title: High-Throughput Time-Series Engine with LSM Compaction Tiering
subtitle: MemTable Sizing, SSTable Compaction Strategies and Bloom Filter Sizing
problem_statement: An IoT telemetry platform ingests 250,000 metric datapoints per second. The storage engine experiences periodic 5-second write stalls (write-stalls) whenever MemTables fill up faster than background threads can perform Leveled Compaction, causing client buffers to overflow.

faded_bug.description: Synchronous disk flushing on caller thread during MemTable saturation triggers massive write stalls.

invariants.description: LSM write stall count must be zero across peak ingest bursts.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Compare Leveled Compaction vs Size-Tiered (Universal) Compaction in terms of Write Amplification, Space Amplification, and Read Amplification.
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: If SSD write endurance is 1 DWPD (Drive Writes Per Day), how does a Write Amplification Factor of 25 impact NVMe hardware lifespan under 250,000 writes/sec?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: A query requests metrics for a non-existent sensor ID. Without Bloom filters, how many disk seeks does an LSM read require across 6 levels?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: We must retain 1 year of metrics. Design downsampling tiers (raw 1s -> 1m -> 1h rollups) that cut storage costs by 85%.

counter_probes.counter_question: Why do traditional B-Trees suffer catastrophic write amplification and random disk I/O when inserting append-heavy time series data at scale?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: B-Trees require in-place page updates, causing random I/O and page splits. LSM-trees convert random writes into sequential append-only disk writes via MemTable flushes.
